To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

7-deazadeoxyguanosine (7dG), an unnatural base analogue of deoxyguanosine, is incorporated into DNA with the same fidelity as deoxyguanosin, 7dG suppresses misincorporation of the unnatural base threosine by the engineered DNA polymerase Therminator, and 7dG suppressor DNA can be transcribed with high efficiency and high fidelity to produce full-length TNA polymers.
7dG can be used to suppress tG:dG Hoogsteen pairing and that the use of 7dG in DNA templates can increase the fidelity of DNA-to-TNA polymerase synthesis.
DNA polymerase-mediated synthesis requires 7-deazaG to suppress G: G mispairing during the transcription of TNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new chemical and biological tools for the study and application of TNA polymers.

the development and characterization of a DNA polymerase that can be used to synthesize large libraries of threose nucleotides, a novel class of nucleic acid polymers that are capable of Darwinian evolution.
the synthesis, replication and evolution of TNA polymers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of 7-deazaG in place of dG in the template strand of TNA transcription allows the synthesis of full length TNA products.
the use of the 7-deazapurine analogue 7dG in the DNA template will suppress the misincorporation of the unnatural nucleotide tGTP and allow the synthesis of full length TNA polymers.
the unnatural base 7-deazguanine (7dG) can suppress the formation of tG:dG pairs in the DNA polymerase active site and allow the efficient synthesis of four-nucleotide-long TNA molecules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method for the synthesis of large, unbiased pools (> 10(6) members) of TNA molecules that contain four nucleotides.
the use of 7-deazaheterocycles in DNA polymerases can improve the fidelity of TNA transcription.
we are the first to demonstrate the synthesis of a four-nucleotide genetic alphabet using a DNA polymerase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
7dG is a useful base analogue for TNA polymerization because it suppresses tGTP mispairing while maintaining the rate of incorporation.
7dG can serve as an alternative base for TNA transcription.
the incorporation of unnatural base analogues into DNA templates can be used to suppress misincorporation events that would otherwise prevent the synthesis of long, full-length TNA polymers.
